Check that districts are consistent across the dataset

Source: R/0_data_quality_checks.R
check_district_consistency.Rd

Checks two things in the merged data: that each district belongs to one admin level 1 unit, and that each district appears in every year of the data. A district that fails either test has usually been renamed or misspelled in part of the workbook.

Usage

check_district_consistency(.data)

Arguments

.data

A data frame. The merged and standardized dataset, with district, adminlevel_1 and year columns.

Value

NULL if no problem is found. Otherwise a character vector with one or two messages, each named "x": one that lists the districts with more than one admin level 1 name, and one that lists the districts missing from at least one year.

Details

Admin level 1 names are compared without regard to case or extra spaces, so "North East" and "north east" count as the same unit. The years a district must appear in are all the distinct years in .data.

Examples

path <- system.file("extdata", "kenya.xlsx", package = "cd2030.core")
data <- load_data(path)
#> ℹ Loading Excel "kenya.xlsx" for parts
#> ! The following columns are empty: anc_1trimester, under5_deaths, total_deaths,
#>   ipv2, measles_cases
#> ℹ Successfully loaded and cleaned data
#> ℹ Auto-detect candidates (|group|): vaccine=19, rmncah=28 -> selected rmncah
check_district_consistency(data)
#> NULL

# A district spelled differently in one year
renamed <- data
renamed$district[renamed$district == "Baringo" & renamed$year == 2023] <- "Baringo County"
check_district_consistency(renamed)
#>                                                                                                    x 
#> "District(s) missing from at least one year present elsewhere in the data: Baringo, Baringo County."
